transcript.text: Alright, let's get started. As we review the NimbusGrid cloud-services agreement, I need both of you to flag any required changes before I can approve this. We've got the business team pushing to execute this month so the migration stays on schedule, but I want to make sure we're not cutting corners on the legal side. Privacy counsel, I'm particularly concerned about the data processing provisions — the current draft permits processing in any country where NimbusGrid operates, and we need to understand the privacy implications of that. Commercial transactions counsel, I want your read on the liability cap and the security incident notice timeline. Both of you — what redlines do we need?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. I completed a data-map review yesterday and confirmed that the platform will process EU employee health information. That review requires three specific changes to the current draft: first, hosting must be restricted to the European Economic Area only — the current 'any country where NimbusGrid operates' provision won't work. Second, the security-incident notice timeline needs to be 72 hours, not the 30 days currently in the draft. And third, we need a vendor deletion certificate within 30 days after termination, which isn't in the draft at all. These aren't optional — they're required given the nature of the data involved.

Based on the business unit's migration-risk assessment and my review of three comparable enterprise agreements this week, we must obtain a $3,000,000 aggregate liability cap — the current $500,000 cap is insufficient. Additionally, we need six months of termination assistance written into the agreement, because our payroll migration cannot be completed in less time than that.
